scope: Theorem 6.3 (Countably many unavailable endpoints) of the manuscript “Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture” (preprints/Koebes-Circle-Domain-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 071 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0080bd36e38b2cd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix any countable coordinate list satisfying (P), and fix β > 0. In the ungated endpoint problem with E = {3R ≤ |z| ≤ 4R}, E∗ = {|z| = 7R/2}, there are at most countably many b ∈ B for which no compatible real barrier u is available with ∥du∥2 + ∥au∥ℓ2(B) < β. Availability permits a countable enlargement of the flags. The prescribed collar sequence may start arbitrarily deep, and the barrier is required to equal one on some collar of that sequence.
